idea.body: A huge or tiny number can be written as one digit times ten to a power. The one digit comes first, from 1 up to 9, followed by a decimal part if needed. 6,300,000 becomes 6.3 x 10^6, since the decimal point moves 6 places to reach one digit in front. A tiny number works the same way but with a negative power: 0.00052 becomes 5.2 x 10^-4. The power of ten tells you exactly how many places, and which direction, the decimal point moved. This makes very large and very small numbers easy to compare and to multiply.

steps: Move the decimal point left until only one digit remains in front of it.
452,000 becomes 4.52 once the point moves 5 places.
Count the places moved: 5, which becomes the power of ten.

ways.name: Move the point and count
ways.when: Use this default method for turning a plain number into scientific notation.
steps: Move the decimal point left until only one digit remains in front.
528000 becomes 5.28 once the point moves 5 places.
Count how many places it moved: 5, which becomes the power of ten.
ways.trap: Writing more than one digit before the decimal point, like 52.8 x 10^4.

ways.name: The powers of ten table
ways.when: Use this to check the power of ten by comparing sizes instead of counting moves.
steps: 0.00073 sits between 10^-4 and 10^-3, so the power of ten is -4.
ways.trap: Picking the power closest in size instead of matching where one digit lands.

The mantissa is above that halfway point, so it rounds up to 10^10.
